title: Writing: My home and my weekend
title_it: Scrittura: la mia casa e il mio weekend
goal: Describe your home with there is / there are, a lot of, much and many and place prepositions, then write a past simple weekend diary.
goal_it: Descrivere la tua casa con there is / there are, a lot of, much e many e preposizioni di luogo, poi scrivere un diario del weekend al past simple.

steps.title: Today: writing about your home and your weekend
steps.title_it: Oggi: scrivere della tua casa e del tuo weekend
en: Today you will write two short texts. First you describe your home or your street. Then you write a diary about last weekend.
For the first text you use there is / there are, a lot of, much and many, and the place prepositions from this week. For the diary you use the past simple.
it: Oggi scrivi due testi brevi. Prima descrivi la tua casa o la tua strada. Poi scrivi un diario del weekend scorso.
Per il primo testo usi there is / there are, a lot of, much e many, e le preposizioni di luogo di questa settimana. Per il diario usi il past simple.

steps.title: Words for home and neighbourhood
en: Learn these ten words and expressions. They are in your flashcards too.
it: Impara queste dieci parole ed espressioni. Le trovi anche nelle flashcard.

steps.title: Model text 1: my home
en: I live in a flat in Bologna, on the second floor. There are two bedrooms, a small kitchen and a bright living room. In the living room there is a sofa opposite the window, and a lamp between the sofa and the bookcase. There isn't much furniture, but there are a lot of books. My street is quiet. There aren't many cars, but there is a lot of noise on Saturday night.
it: Vivo in un appartamento a Bologna, al secondo piano. Ci sono due camere da letto, una piccola cucina e un soggiorno luminoso. Nel soggiorno c'è un divano di fronte alla finestra e una lampada tra il divano e la libreria. Non c'è molto arredamento, ma ci sono molti libri. La mia strada è tranquilla. Non ci sono molte auto, ma il sabato sera c'è molto rumore.

steps.title: Model text 2: a weekend diary
steps.title_it: Testo modello 2: il diario del weekend
en: Sunday evening. On Saturday I got up late and had a big breakfast. Then I went to the market with my sister, and we bought vegetables and cheese. In the afternoon I didn't study. I met two friends at a cafe and we talked for hours. In the evening we cooked pasta and watched a film. It was a lovely day.
it: Domenica sera. Sabato mi sono alzato tardi e ho fatto una colazione abbondante. Poi sono andato al mercato con mia sorella e abbiamo comprato verdura e formaggio. Nel pomeriggio non ho studiato. Ho incontrato due amici in un bar e abbiamo chiacchierato per ore. La sera abbiamo cucinato la pasta e guardato un film. È stata una giornata bellissima.

steps.title: Checklist before you write
en: Use this list to check every sentence, then read your text again.
it: Usa questa lista per controllare ogni frase, poi rileggi il testo.

head: Check
Example
rows: There is + singular or uncountable; there are + plural
There is a bank. There are two shops.
There isn't much space. There aren't many shops.
A lot of works with both, and is good in positive sentences
There are a lot of trees. There is a lot of noise.
Place prepositions: in, on, at, between, opposite, next to
The lamp is between the sofa and the bookcase.
Past simple diary: finished time (last weekend, on Saturday)
Negative and question: didn't / did + base verb
I didn't study. Did you see Anna?
Order words: first, then, after that, in the evening
First I shopped, then I cooked.

steps.q: There ___ two bedrooms in my flat.
steps.q_it: Nel mio appartamento ci sono due camere da letto.
steps.why: Two bedrooms is plural, so we use there are.
steps.why_it: Two bedrooms è plurale, quindi there are.

steps.q: There ___ a supermarket opposite the station.
steps.q_it: C'è un supermercato di fronte alla stazione.
steps.why: A supermarket is singular: there is (there's).
steps.why_it: A supermarket è singolare: there is (there's).

steps.q: How ___ traffic is there in your street?
steps.q_it: Quanto traffico c'è nella tua strada?
steps.why: Traffic is uncountable, so we ask how much.
steps.why_it: Traffic è uncountable, quindi si chiede how much.

steps.q: There aren't ___ shops in my village. (much / many)
steps.q_it: Nel mio paese non ci sono molti negozi.
steps.why: Shops is countable and plural: not many.
steps.why_it: Shops è countable plurale: not many.

steps.q: There is ___ noise at night, so I sleep badly.
steps.q_it: Di notte c'è molto rumore, quindi dormo male.
steps.why: Noise is uncountable. A lot of works with uncountable nouns, many does not.
steps.why_it: Noise è uncountable. A lot of va bene con gli uncountable, many no.

steps.q: I haven't got ___ furniture in my room. (much / many)
steps.q_it: Non ho molti mobili nella mia camera.
steps.why: Furniture is uncountable: not much.
steps.why_it: Furniture è uncountable: not much.

steps.q: Put the words in order.
steps.q_it: Metti le parole in ordine.
answers: There are a lot of trees in the park
steps.why: There are + a lot of + plural noun, then the place.
steps.why_it: There are + a lot of + nome plurale, poi il luogo.

steps.q: The lamp hangs ___ the table, but it doesn't touch it.
steps.q_it: La lampada è appesa sopra il tavolo, ma non lo tocca.
steps.why: Over (or above) means higher up without touching. On means touching.
steps.why_it: Over (o above) significa più in alto, senza toccare. On significa a contatto.

steps.q: My bed is ___ the window and the wardrobe.
steps.q_it: Il mio letto è tra la finestra e l'armadio.
steps.why: Between is for two things, one on each side.
steps.why_it: Between si usa per due cose, una per lato.

steps.q: The bank is ___ the post office, on the other side of the street.
steps.q_it: La banca è di fronte all'ufficio postale, dall'altra parte della strada.
steps.why: Opposite means facing something across a space.
steps.why_it: Opposite significa di fronte, con uno spazio in mezzo.

steps.q: I live ___ 15 Mill Road.
steps.q_it: Abito al numero 15 di Mill Road.
steps.why: With a full address (a number and a street) we use at.
steps.why_it: Con un indirizzo completo (numero e via) si usa at.

steps.q: My flat is ___ the third floor.
steps.q_it: Il mio appartamento è al terzo piano.
steps.why: Floors take on: on the third floor.
steps.why_it: I piani vogliono on: on the third floor.

steps.q: Put the words in order.
steps.q_it: Metti le parole in ordine.
answers: The bus stop is next to the library
steps.why: Subject + is + next to + place.
steps.why_it: Soggetto + is + next to + luogo.

steps.q: On Saturday I ___ (go) to the market with my sister.
steps.q_it: Sabato sono andato al mercato con mia sorella.
steps.why: Saturday is finished time, so past simple. Go is irregular: went.
steps.why_it: Sabato è un tempo finito, quindi past simple. Go è irregolare: went.

steps.q: We ___ (not / watch) TV on Sunday.
steps.q_it: Domenica non abbiamo guardato la TV.
steps.why: Negative past simple: didn't + base verb.
steps.why_it: Negativa del past simple: didn't + verbo base.

steps.q: Put the words in order.
steps.q_it: Metti le parole in ordine.
answers: We cooked a big lunch for the family
steps.why: Subject + past verb + object + for ...
steps.why_it: Soggetto + verbo al passato + complemento + for ...

steps.q: Which sentence is correct for a diary?
steps.q_it: Quale frase è corretta per un diario?
options: Yesterday I have visited my aunt.
Yesterday I did visited my aunt.
steps.why: Yesterday is a finished time, so past simple. Not the present perfect, and not did + past.
steps.why_it: Yesterday è un tempo finito, quindi past simple. Non il present perfect, e non did + passato.

steps.q: It ___ (be) sunny on Saturday, so we went to the beach.
steps.q_it: Sabato c'era il sole, quindi siamo andati in spiaggia.
steps.why: Be in the past: it was.
steps.why_it: Be al passato: it was.

steps.q: What time ___ you get up on Sunday?
steps.q_it: A che ora ti sei alzato domenica?
steps.why: Past question: did + subject + base verb.
steps.why_it: Domanda al passato: did + soggetto + verbo base.

steps.q: Which sentence has a mistake?
steps.q_it: Quale frase ha un errore?
options: I didn't went out on Friday.
steps.why: After didn't we use the base verb: I didn't go out.
steps.why_it: Dopo didn't si usa il verbo base: I didn't go out.

steps.q: First I had a shower, ___ I had breakfast.
steps.q_it: Prima ho fatto la doccia, poi ho fatto colazione.
steps.why: Then (or after that) puts events in order.
steps.why_it: Then (o after that) mette gli eventi in ordine.

steps.q: Put the words in order.
steps.q_it: Metti le parole in ordine.
answers: Did you see your friends at the weekend
steps.why: Did + subject + base verb + the rest.
steps.why_it: Did + soggetto + verbo base + il resto.

steps.q: Yesterday I ___ my keys at the cinema.
steps.q_it: Ieri ho perso le chiavi al cinema.
steps.why: Yesterday is a definite time in the past: past simple.
steps.why_it: Yesterday è un momento passato definito: past simple.

steps.q: I've just ___ my room, so it looks tidy.
steps.q_it: Ho appena pulito la mia camera, quindi è in ordine.
steps.why: Have just + past participle: the result is clear now.
steps.why_it: Have just + participio passato: il risultato si vede adesso.

steps.q: We were having dinner ___ the phone rang.
steps.q_it: Stavamo cenando quando ha squillato il telefono.
steps.why: When introduces the short action (the phone rang) that interrupts the long one.
steps.why_it: When introduce l'azione breve (il telefono ha squillato) che interrompe quella lunga.

steps.title: Your writing task
en: Part 1. Describe your home or your street in six to eight sentences. Use there is / there are at least twice, a lot of once, not much or not many once, and two place prepositions.
Part 2. Write a diary about last weekend in six sentences. Use the past simple, one negative sentence and two linking words (first, then, after that).
Write on paper or in your notes app. This app does not correct your text, so read it again with the checklist and check each sentence.
If you want, share your text with a friend from the class and compare.
it: Parte 1. Descrivi la tua casa o la tua strada in sei otto frasi. Usa there is / there are almeno due volte, a lot of una volta, not much o not many una volta e due preposizioni di luogo.
Parte 2. Scrivi un diario del weekend scorso in sei frasi. Usa il past simple, una frase negativa e due parole di collegamento (first, then, after that).
Scrivi su carta o nell'app note. L'app non corregge il testo, quindi rileggilo con la checklist e controlla ogni frase.
Se vuoi, condividi il testo con un compagno del corso e confrontatelo.

cards.ex: The sofa is in the living room.
My clothes are in the wardrobe.
The lamp is next to the bookcase.
The street is noisy at night.
There are a lot of cafes here.
They live on the second floor.
At the weekend I see my friends.
First I shopped, then I cooked.
Last weekend we went to the lake.
